synth.title: Richness/restraint calibration prior (how much to put on a surface)
synth.principle_summary: How much to put on a first-draft surface is governed by two layers that must be applied together, not one. The COGNITIVE layer (unchanged from the academic pass) sets a numeric ceiling: 4 to 7 Gestalt-grouped chunks above the fold (Miller 1956 ceiling, Cowan 2001 floor of roughly 3-5), with the aesthetic-usability effect and 50ms first-impression research explaining why spending the marginal unit on finish reads as competence, not decoration. The STRUCTURAL layer, newly corroborated across seven real shipped apps (Fresha, Treatwell, Square Go, Urban Company, CVS Health, Airbnb, Airtasker), shows the ceiling is not spent as a flat page-wide imagery percentage. Every real competitor concentrates imagery into ONE zone sized to that surface's TASK TYPE (a hero/PDP carousel runs 35-45% of first viewport, a browse card runs close to the existing Solen 1/3 floor, a checkout or slot-picker surface runs near zero) and goes flat, text-only, list-row below that zone. Fresha's own above-the-fold service cap (6 of 22 shown) lands inside the independently-derived 4-7 chunk band, which is the strongest single piece of corroboration in this synthesis: a competitor's real UI decision and a 70-year-old cognitive-load literature converge on the same number by two unrelated methods. The direction to lean when a mockup is ambiguous is not a blanket "richer is safer" rule (that leg of the academic draft was already downgraded to T3); real evidence instead conditions it on TASK TYPE, browse/discovery screens tolerate and reward more richness (Too Good To Go, Airtasker, Sephora), transactional/booking-task screens (CVS slot picker, Urban Company cart, Square Go PDP) stay sparse and still read as competent, so "lean richer" only applies inside a browse/discovery surface, never inside a commit-flow step. 2026 design-press trend claims toward denser, more decorative "maximalism" (bento grids, tactile maximalism) are real directional signal but stay T3/CONV and are explicitly NOT adopted where they would loosen Solen's 80/17 restraint or no-decorative-artifact law; they are noted as a live tension, not a license.
synth.proposed_addition:
GENERATIVE PRIOR (closes gap register G1, RATIONALE.md:826), revises and extends the section-28 anchor / cross-ref near section 12 (Berlyne line 185) with real-app corroboration layered onto the academic bands. Cross-reference PSYCHOLOGY.md law 7 ("Photos are the decision input, not decoration", T1 causal, +9% Airbnb occupancy) for the behavioral WHY behind the imagery floor; this prior does not re-derive that claim.

1. IMAGERY IS A ZONE, NOT A FLAT PERCENTAGE. The FLOORS LAW's "~1/3 imagery" (CONV, owner-approved 2026-07-21) is confirmed as the right browse-card number by real precedent, but it must be SCOPED by surface type, not applied as a page-wide constant. Concrete bands, corroborated by direct product observation:
   - Hero/PDP surfaces: one photo zone at roughly 35-45% of first viewport (Fresha salon PDP carousel ~40-45%; Airbnb detail hero: one large photo at 50% width plus a 2x2 grid of four smaller photos, 5 photos total), then a hard cut to flat white/text below with zero further imagery in the repeating content (Fresha's own services tab runs fully text-only rows below the hero, no thumbnail per service).
   - Browse/list card surfaces: the existing ~1/3 floor stands unchanged.
   - Transactional/commit-flow surfaces (checkout, cart, slot-picker): imagery drops to near zero and this is CORRECT, not a violation. Urban Company's cart, Square Go's service-detail PDP, and CVS Health's slot picker all ship at or near 0% imagery and read as competent, not broken, real-world evidence that runs directly counter to a flat imagery percentage. This closes the exact gap the earlier academic-only pass left cross-referenced but never scoped.

2. CHUNK COUNT ABOVE THE FOLD: 4 to 7 distinct Gestalt-grouped chunks, biased low (4-5) on a glance-based mobile surface (unchanged from the verified academic band: Miller 1956 T1 ceiling, Cowan 2001 T2 floor of roughly 3-5). NEW CORROBORATION: Fresha's own above-the-fold service list shows 6 of 22 total services before a "See all" overflow, landing inside this band by independent real-world observation, not cognitive-load theory. Treat this as the strongest evidence point in the whole prior: two unrelated methods (a shipped competitor's product decision and 1956-2001 cognitive-load literature) converge on the same number.

3. DECORATIVE-VS-INFORMATIONAL GATE inside a chunk: unchanged, still the copy-economy delete-test (project CLAUDE.md rule 1), always outranks richness. NEW BOUND: three independent competitor teardowns (Fresha, Treatwell, Booksy's own documented component list) converge on the SAME roughly seven-item component vocabulary for a marketplace profile (cover photo/gallery, name plus rating plus count, description, services with price plus duration, staff, reviews, one booking CTA) with no decorative filler beyond that set. This is evidence the informational ceiling is not just theoretically derivable, it is what real competitors independently converged on without a shared design system.

4. DIRECTIONAL BIAS WHEN UNCERTAIN IS TASK-CONDITIONED, NOT BLANKET. Revises the earlier academic-only band, which leaned on a Reinecke and Gajos 2014 asymmetric-curve claim that could not be verified from the paper's actual findings and was downgraded to a hedged T3 lean. Real-app evidence gives a sharper, task-conditioned rule instead of a single global lean:
   - Inside a BROWSE/DISCOVERY surface, lean richer up to band 2's ceiling. Too Good To Go's discover feed (photo ~55% of card height, badge, strikethrough-plus-bold price, distance) and Airtasker's category feed (image-forward cards immediately followed by an icon-only pill grid on the same screen) both ship dense and legible because every element is bound to a fixed grid position, never floating.
   - Inside a TRANSACTIONAL/COMMIT-FLOW surface (any booking step, cart, checkout, slot picker), lean sparser, near the floor of band 2, not the ceiling. CVS Health's slot picker and Urban Company's cart both under-fill by Solen's own richness instinct and still read as competent precisely because the task is narrow and the user's attention should not be split.
   - This directly maps onto Solen's own booking flow (services, staff, time, pay): earlier steps (services list, staff picker) may sit toward band 2's richer end; Zeit and Bezahlen should sit toward the sparse end. This is new, generative guidance the earlier academic-only draft did not produce.
   - Confidence note carried forward: this band replaces a downgraded T2 citation with T3-tier competitor observation; still the weakest-evidenced band in the prior, now on firmer footing than before but still pending the Taste Lab probe below.

5. NOVELTY BUDGET: unchanged from the verified academic band. MAYA (T2, confirmed) caps genuinely-new pattern to ONE differentiator per surface; reuse a LOCKED component everywhere else. The band-3 component-vocabulary convergence (Fresha/Treatwell/Booksy) is independent real-world support for the same discipline: none of the three competitors invented a novel eighth building block.

6. DENSITY/WHITESPACE COUPLING, extended with a concrete grouping mechanic. TASTE_DASHBOARDS.md finding 14 (CONV, confirmed, currently scoped to dashboard tables/forms) still applies to any browse card: rising field count must pair with growing, not shrinking, gutters. NEW, CONV-tier lever from 2026 design-press scouting: bento-style modular grid grouping (asymmetric tile sizing inside one shared grid, T3 trend, not a validated study) is the one trend-research finding compatible with Solen's restraint law, because it raises perceived richness through LAYOUT variety, not through added color or decoration, and it is exactly the mechanic Too Good To Go and Fresha rely on to keep dense cards legible (every element bound to a grid slot). Offered as an implementation technique for band 1 and band 4's richer end, not as a new numeric floor.

7. FINISH ALLOCATION (where, not how much): unchanged, still CONV, still an allocation order not a quantity prior (RESTRAINT_TEST.md, RATIONALE.md:189).

8. TENSION FLAG, NOT ADOPTED: 2026 design-press "dense is back" and "tactile maximalism" trend claims (T3, MyDesigner Blog, AuFaitUX, Medium/Bootcamp roundups) and Sephora's card imagery ratio (~55-60% per card, saturated illustrated color blocks) both point toward more visual density and MORE decorative color-and-texture richness than Solen's 80/17 near-monochrome law and no-decorative-artifact rule permit. These are logged as a live directional tension in the field, not evidence for loosening any LOCKFILE literal. The one counter-trend that is directionally ALIGNED with Solen's existing restraint (Envato/GitNexa "calm design", narrative-over-density dashboards) is the citable trend if this prior is ever challenged as too sparse.

BOUNDARY: this prior sets a first-draft band for a NEW mockup only; it reopens no frozen literal (card radius, LOCKFILE spacing tokens, the 44px touch floor, the 80/17 ratio, the no-decorative-artifact rule); band 3's informational gate always outranks band 4's richness bias when they conflict; band 4's task-conditioning always outranks a blanket richer-lean.
synth.generative_prior:
Concrete defaults for a first-draft mockup, stated as bands with the real apps that demonstrate each number:

- IMAGERY ZONE (not a flat ratio): hero/PDP surfaces run one photo zone at 35-45% of first viewport (Fresha salon PDP carousel ~40-45%; Airbnb detail hero 1 large photo at 50% width + 2x2 grid of 4 smaller = 5 photos total), browse/list cards hold the existing Solen ~1/3 floor, transactional/commit-flow surfaces (cart, checkout, slot picker) run near 0% imagery (Urban Company cart, Square Go PDP, CVS Health slot picker, all zero-photo and still competent).
- CHUNK CEILING: 4-7 Gestalt-grouped chunks above the fold, biased 4-5 on mobile (Miller 1956 T1 / Cowan 2001 T2). Corroborated live: Fresha shows exactly 6 of 22 services before "See all" overflow, inside this band.
- COMPONENT VOCABULARY CEILING: roughly 7 building blocks for a marketplace profile page (photo/gallery, name+rating+count, description, services w/ price+duration, staff, reviews, one CTA), independently converged on by Fresha, Treatwell, and Booksy's own documented spec, no decorative filler beyond this set in any of the three.
- DIRECTION WHEN UNCERTAIN, task-conditioned: lean richer up to the ceiling inside a browse/discovery surface (Too Good To Go feed cards ~55% photo, Airtasker image-forward carousel immediately followed by an icon-only pill grid on the same screen); lean sparser toward the floor inside a transactional/commit-flow surface (CVS slot picker, Urban Company cart, Square Go PDP, all near-zero imagery and text-first, still read as competent because the task is narrow).
- GRID-BINDING as the density-without-clutter mechanic: every element in a dense real-app surface (Too Good To Go, Fresha) is bound to a fixed grid position, never floating; bento-style modular grouping (T3 trend) is the closest named technique for this in current design-press vocabulary.

synth.taste_lab_probe:
Build 3 real variants of ONE already-shipped Solen browse surface (recommend salon SearchTemplate grid, highest-traffic customer surface already wired for the FLOORS LAW 5-pass note), structure untouched, only richness dialed, PLUS a second paired probe on one transactional step (recommend the booking Zeit step) to test the new task-conditioned direction band.

Probe A (browse surface, tests bands 1, 2, 4-richer-leg):
- Level A sparse: imagery on ~15% of cards, 2 facts per card, flat depth.
- Level B target: imagery ~1/3 per the existing floor, 3-4 facts, gray-tray on photo-less cards, band 6 grid-binding applied.
- Level C cluttered: imagery on every card plus one decorative graphic, 6+ facts, tight gutters, one non-informational badge (this level intentionally probes the Sephora/Too-Good-To-Go boundary named in band 8).

Probe B (transactional surface, tests band 4-sparser-leg, new in this synthesis):
- Level A minimal: current Zeit step as-is, near-zero imagery, text/pill-first (matches CVS/Urban Company precedent).
- Level B slightly richer: add one contextual photo or richer slot-card treatment, still inside band 2's low end (4-5 chunks).
- Level C dense: pack additional metadata/imagery onto the slot picker, tests whether richness on a commit-flow step actually hurts task completion the way real-app precedent predicts.

Procedure, both probes: show all 3 unlabeled at real mobile width (375px). Ask (1) unprompted pairwise preference plus one-sentence why, (2) a squint-test chunk count on the winner. For Probe A, also ask which level "feels like Solen" vs which level "feels like a different app" to directly test the Sephora/maximalism boundary. For Probe B, additionally time-to-first-tap on the slot grid across levels, since band 4's task-conditioning predicts B/A should outperform C on speed even if C wins raw preference. Record both winners' exact chunk counts and imagery percentages back into RATIONALE.md, replacing this prior's placeholder bands with owner-confirmed numbers, and log whether Probe B confirms or refutes the task-conditioned direction rule in band 4 before that band is treated as settled.

myths_caught: Fresha 'six of 22 services shown above the fold' called out as the strongest corroboration point in the synthesis does not reproduce: an independent re-fetch of the same live URL returned 4 shown before 'See all', not 6. The claim is downgraded to a range and the 'strongest evidence point' superlative is removed; the band-4-7 fit still holds (at the floor) but is not the clean convergence the draft claimed.

The 50ms first-impression citation is likely swapped: the well-established primary source for '50ms to form a first impression of a webpage' is Lindgaard, Fernandes, Dudek, Brown (2006), not Tuch et al. (2012) IJHCS. The draft's own note says it 'corrected' an earlier hci-basel.ch/2007 citation to Tuch 2012, but Tuch's own lab is hosted at hci-basel.ch and the paper's actual exposure duration could not be confirmed (access blocked). Repointed the 50ms claim to Lindgaard 2006; kept Tuch 2012 as a narrower, duration-unspecified claim.

Treatwell '~60% text / 40% visual' self-estimate does not reproduce: an independent re-fetch of the same page estimated 80-85% text / 15-20% visual. Both are ungrounded LLM eyeball estimates, not pixel measurements. Softened to a qualitative claim, tier CONV to T3.

Booksy's documented profile structure does not explicitly itemize 'staff photos' as a discrete block (only 'portfolio / showcase your best work'); softened from an exact 7-item match to an approximate one.

Uber 'internal design critique flagged as info present but not prioritized' is an unverifiable narrative claim sourced only to a tertiary teardown site, not a primary Uber document; downgraded CONV to T3 and flagged as weak, not cut, since it does not carry independent weight in the prior anyway.
verified.residual_risks: Owner-decision items: (1) the imagery-zone bands (35-45% hero, ~1/3 browse floor, ~0% transactional) are real-app-observed but still CONV/T3 tier, not causal evidence; they should go through the taste_lab_probe before being written into RATIONALE.md as anything firmer than a first-draft prior. (2) Band 4's task-conditioned direction rule (richer in browse, sparser in transactional) is the weakest-evidenced band per the draft's own admission and explicitly depends on Probe B to confirm or refute before being treated as settled; do not let it silently harden into a rule before that probe runs. (3) The bento-grid / tactile-maximalism tension flag in point 8 is correctly logged as NOT adopted, but is a live directional pull against the 80/17 near-monochrome law; if a future designer leans on 2026 trend pieces to loosen restraint, point 8 needs to be re-read as a boundary, not permission. (4) The Airbnb +9% occupancy figure was not independently re-verified in this pass (search access exhausted); it is inherited from PSYCHOLOGY.md law 7 per the draft's own stated boundary, so re-verification responsibility sits with that file's own audit trail, not this stream. (5) All Mobbin-sourced screen observations (Square Go, Urban Company, CVS Health, Sephora, Too Good To Go, Airtasker) are single-example, T3, and unverifiable by me directly (no Mobbin access); they read as internally consistent with the task-conditioned theory but should be treated as illustrative, not proof, until a second independent screenshot pass confirms them. (6) Live-page WebFetch counts (Fresha service count, Treatwell text/visual ratio) proved unstable across two independent fetches in this session alone; any RATIONALE.md number sourced this way should carry a 'measured via automated fetch, not a fixed screenshot count, recheck before treating as precise' caveat rather than being presented as a hard number.

NEW, T3-tier lever from 2026 design-press scouting: bento-style modular grid grouping (asymmetric tile sizing inside one shared grid, T3 trend, not a validated study) is the one trend-research finding compatible with Solen's restraint law, because it raises perceived richness through LAYOUT variety, not through added color or decoration, and it is exactly the mechanic Too Good To Go and Fresha appear to rely on to keep dense cards legible (single-example T3 observation). Offered as an implementation technique for band 1 and band 4's richer end, not as a new numeric floor.

7. FINISH ALLOCATION (where, not how much): unchanged, still CONV, still an allocation order not a quantity prior (RESTRAINT_TEST.md, RATIONALE.md:189).

8. TENSION FLAG, NOT ADOPTED: 2026 design-press "dense is back" and "tactile maximalism" trend claims (T3, MyDesigner Blog, AuFaitUX, Medium/Bootcamp roundups) and Sephora's card imagery ratio (~55-60% per card, saturated illustrated color blocks, T3 single-example) both point toward more visual density and MORE decorative color-and-texture richness than Solen's 80/17 near-monochrome law and no-decorative-artifact rule permit. These are logged as a live directional tension in the field, not evidence for loosening any LOCKFILE literal. The one counter-trend that is directionally ALIGNED with Solen's existing restraint (Envato/GitNexa "calm design", narrative-over-density dashboards) is the citable trend if this prior is ever challenged as too sparse.

BOUNDARY: this prior sets a first-draft band for a NEW mockup only; it reopens no frozen literal (card radius, LOCKFILE spacing tokens, the 44px touch floor, the 80/17 ratio, the no-decorative-artifact rule); band 3's informational gate always outranks band 4's richness bias when they conflict; band 4's task-conditioning always outranks a blanket richer-lean; no number in this prior should be treated as more precise than T3/CONV tier until the taste_lab_probe returns owner-confirmed counts.
